explanation:
### How it works

The array stores the next available number, while −1 marks an allocated number. Allocation removes the head of the free list and release inserts a number back at its head.

### Steps

1. Initialize a circular chain of available numbers.
2. On get, remove the current free head and mark it allocated.
3. Check availability using the marker.
4. Release an allocated number by linking it before the current head.

### Complexity

- Time: O(N) construction; O(1) per operation for N phone numbers.
- Space: O(N) for the free-list array.

alternatives.explanation:
### How it works

Keep the available numbers directly in a set. Any available number may be returned, so set removal is enough for allocation.

### Steps

1. Initialize the set with all valid numbers.
2. Pop an arbitrary number on get, or return −1 when empty.
3. Check set membership.
4. Release by adding the number back.

### Complexity

- Time: O(N) construction; expected O(1) per operation.
- Space: O(N) for available numbers.
